papers.working_title: Gaussian-driven wave evolutions and uniform spectral growth
papers.central_question: Can physical-time Gaussian phase evolutions and their long-time operator products be treated by a reusable theorem, with estimates uniform in an expanding spatial localization?
papers.existing_material: Sections16-24 and29-37: both wave variances, actual original-W driver, regularization limits, phase Young evolution, signed spectral forms, symplectic baseline, Gaussian tubes and uniform products; exact grouping subject to semantic dependency audit.
candidate_theorems: For original H:homog, d1/2/3 and alpha+alpha0<2, fixed smooth physical mask and finite horizon: same-W Gaussian compact-operator path on E=H^(1/2)xH^(-1/2), Holder exponent theta>1/2, sqrt(p) path moments; actual regularizations converge and identify the physical two-component Young flow.

An abstract Gaussian Laplace upper principle for families of long-time wave endpoint functionals on varying spaces/localizations: hypotheses must specify actual Cameron maps, concentration/typical-radius control, subquadratic coarse envelopes and uniform deterministic product-rate approximation. Lower conclusions require a separate nonvanishing observable argument, not mere operator norm growth.
papers.additional_value_test: Verify the abstract interfaces in a second meaningful class, starting with finite positive sums of admissible homogeneous spatial covariances of different orders. This extension is proposed, not proved.
papers.independence_gate: No use of intrinsic C2 theorem or positive-score finiteness as a premise. Separate standard Young/Gaussian facts from the wave-specific variance and uniformity estimates. A restatement of standard contraction principles is insufficient.
papers.publication_gate: Exact source-theorem and solution-topology comparison, independent audit and useful standalone theorem. If these fail, retain as the methods section of paperII instead of forcing a separate paper.

first_targets: Start with actual even moment p4. Define Cp from E|u|^p at the same time scale and test whether Cp=(p/2)^((4-alpha)/(3-alpha))*C2. Score homogeneity already known algebraically does NOT prove this moment identity. Need actual p-chain source/mask estimates, correct point transfer and positive terminal-observable lower bound.

For covariance Gamma1+Gamma2 with distinct homogeneous orders, test whether the larger order governs the leading growth exponent and whether its own variational constant survives addition of the lower-order component. Individual self-similarity is lost for the sum; do not reuse exact scaling without a replacement.

Later separate short-time covariance singularity from long-time memory. Compare power-law and tempered power-law temporal kernels; pose the growth/crossover question without asserting the present kappa formula persists.
